problem: Generate dense, failure-sensitive policy improvement signals for contact-rich multistage tasks without simulating entire terminal trajectories.
contribution: RISE composes a controllable video dynamics model with a separately learned progress/TD value model, then trains an advantage-conditioned policy on imagined and real data. Physical data, expert demonstrations and human corrections remain essential anchors.
algorithm: Adapt Genie Envisioner with action encoder, stronger context noise and task-centric batches. Initialize value backbone from pi0.5; warm up temporal progress regression then combine TD targets with terminal±1 labels. Score an action chunk by mean predicted future value minus current value. Condition pi0.5 on discretized advantage, propose actions at optimal advantage, relabel with learned evaluated advantage and flow-match proposed actions. Mix offline data and use EMA rollout policy; at most two consecutive imagined chunks limit compounding error.
observations: Multiview images, language and task-specific action/state recordings; successful/failed rollouts and human corrective data. Progress value is learned from trajectory timing plus outcome labels and can inherit labeling or imagination bias.
actions: Absolute joint control on dual AgileX arms described as7DoF. Advantage labels guide flow-policy actions; this is not an embodiment-agnostic executable motor representation. World/value models operate during training only, with no added deployment inference overhead.
embodiment_and_data: Real dynamic conveyor brick sorting, backpack packing and box closing; AgibotWorld/Galaxea dynamics pretraining.16H100 GPUs7days pretraining,8H100 GPUs3days task adaptation, value training8GPUs1day; policy stages also8GPUs. Exact physical evaluation denominator NOT_EXTRACTED in inspected main text.
experiments: Compare task success and stage scores, real/offline mixture, generated states/actions, task-centric batches, progress andTD losses. All ablations use difficult brick sorting. RECAP is ported to pi0.5 because originalpi0.6 is inaccessible; not an official checkpoint equivalence result.
baselines: Pi0.5,DAgger,PPO,DSRL and reimplemented RECAP with close stated compute budgets. Real correction data vary by training regime, so inspect data composition before attributing all gain to imagination.
quantitative_result: TableI PDFp6:RISE success85/85/95% across sorting/backpack/box versusRECAP50/40/60%. TableIIp7 offline ratio0.1 gives5%complete versus50%at0.6 and30%at0.9, showing sensitivity. TableVp7 real-task FVD full66.84 versus61.22 without task-centric batching is a negative metric despite improvedEPE0.54 versus0.68; do not repeat universal all-metric superiority.
limitations: Rare transitions can remain physically implausible; learned value/reward may misrank. Nontrivial real data and tuned real/synthetic balance remain necessary. Compute cost is high and extends beyond policy training. Two-chunk imagination is explicitly limited; successful stage scores are not full task success or grasp verification.
code_and_license: Primary project https://opendrivelab.com/RISE . Code, models and datasets licenses not independently inspected; pretrained GE/pi0.5/data rights remain separate. No code inspected/executed.
